A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FragFM and retain identifiable corresponding methods, experiments, and appendices. Text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support comparison despite substantial revision and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original FragFM generation, reconstruction, sampling-efficiency, and conditional-generation results on MOSES, GuacaMol, and COCONUT, including Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 reports original FragFM benchmark and conditioning experiments, including docking-score conditioning, plus dataset analyses and repeated-run results in its appendices.

M1.justification: v1 constructs bags from sampled molecules, uses a uniform fragment prior, and applies classifier-free guidance. v2 specifies a masked fragment prior, marginal-fragment bag sampling at each Euler step, and classifier guidance combined with property-weighted bag selection (Sections 3.3–3.4; Appendix A.4). These change the generation procedure; the autoencoder and Blossom reconstruction backbone remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds ZINC250K generation conditioned on docking scores for FA7, JAK2, and PARP1. MOSES conditioning retains logP, QED, and ring count but removes TPSA. NPGen continues the existing COCONUT-based natural-product task rather than introducing an entirely new domain.

E2.justification: The natural-product comparison expands from DiGress alone to DiGress, GraphAF, JT-VAE, and HierVAE (Table 2 in both versions). Standard benchmark tables also add plain Cometh alongside Cometh-PC. The GuacaMol row called Cometh in v1 matches v2's Cometh-PC scores and should not be treated as a removed comparator.

E3.justification: The processed natural-product dataset changes from 416,249 to 658,566 molecules, and evaluation increases from 10,000 to 30,000 generated molecules. v1 specifies an 85:5:10 split; v2 states 85:5:15, but its counts imply approximately 80:5:15 (Appendix D.1). v2 also changes the stated NP comparison reference from training to test data and replaces the common noise parameter 0.1 with dataset-specific node/edge values.

E4.justification: v2 adds fragment-bag guidance-strength analysis, MAE–validity robustness plots, NPGen property-distribution and UMAP analyses, and broader baseline failure cases. It extends test-fragment generalization evaluation to GuacaMol. MOSES test-fragment comparisons, reconstruction accuracy, and sampling-step sensitivity already appeared in v1 and are retained or revised.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without run counts. v2 newly reports three-run averaging for FragFM's standard benchmarks and generalization comparisons, and means with standard deviations for every NPGen model in Table 3. Because v1's run count is unspecified, an actual increase in runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: Results are extensively revised or added. MOSES training-fragment FCD changes from 0.71 to 0.58; GuacaMol FragFM KL score changes from 99.6 to 97.4, now below DeFoG's 97.7. Natural-product validity changes from 92.2 to 98.0 and FCD from 1.21 to 1.34 under revised benchmark conditions. Docking results are new, and runtimes change. These are not uniformly comparable performance gains. Reconstruction accuracy entries remain identical.

T1.justification: v2 adds an Info-NCE density-ratio formulation, conditional-bag derivations, a diffusion-bridge limiting argument for continuous flow matching, and explicit detailed-balance rates. These substantially extend v1's mathematics. However, the symmetric node rates in v2 Eq. 40 fail its Eq. 38 balance condition for masked-prior probabilities t and 1−t, except at t=0.5.

C1.justification: Fragment-bag control changes from future work in v1's conclusion to an achieved contribution emphasized throughout v2. v2 also strengthens reconstruction claims to 'without information loss' and 'lossless,' whereas v1 describes accurate reconstruction. The central claims of efficient fragment-based generation and improved property control remain.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets NPGen's chemical-space distributions, explains additional baseline failures through chemical instability or restricted structural diversity, and discusses how bag composition limits attainable properties. Section 3.4 also acknowledges that bag-averaged sampling only approximates the desired posterior. v1's existing scaffold-coverage limitation is retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies optimizer settings, learning rate, gradient clipping, EMA, A100 training budgets, checkpoint selection, auxiliary features, and loss weights. It adds the COCONUT snapshot date, baseline implementation links and adaptations, and docking-oracle details. These substantially expand v1's sparse reproducibility information, without establishing that every newly documented setting changed.

R1.justification: Beyond relocating related work, v2 broadens discussion of autoregressive graph generators and adds literature supporting Info-NCE, diffusion bridges, natural-product characteristics, and benchmark design. It positions NPGen against limitations and claimed saturation of standard drug-like benchmarks. Some earlier image, text, video, and SMILES-generation references and discussion are removed.

P1.justification: The introduction, framework exposition, results discussion, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Related work moves into the main text, training and generation receive separate explanations, NPGen receives a dedicated section, and the appendices are extensively reorganized. The title and author block also change.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the earlier architecture schematics with a main-text overview and redrawn parameterization diagram, redesigns benchmark tables, and redraws conditioning plots with changed axes and legends. It adds dataset-distribution, UMAP, validity, docking, and baseline molecule panels. The MOSES fragment display shrinks from 100 to 50 entries, alongside new GuacaMol and NPGen fragment displays.

improvement.justification: Additional NPGen baselines, docking and bag-control experiments, uncertainty reporting, and implementation details substantially strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. However, v2's new node-rate formula contradicts its detailed-balance condition, its NPGen split ratios contradict the listed counts, and its lossless claims exceed the retained reconstruction accuracies. The PDFs do not establish whether the sampler inconsistency is only a printed error or affects the experiments, preventing a reliable judgment of the net quality change.
